field.label: Drop query types
field.help: Record types Blocky answers with an empty response instead of forwarding, e.g. AAAA to suppress IPv6 answers on an IPv4-only network.

field.label: Sources
field.help: Hosts files used for name resolution: an http or https URL, /etc/hosts, a file in /usr/local/etc/blocky/lists, or inline content. Anything else is written as an inline entry rather than a file name. Entries are answered directly by Blocky.

field.label: Hosts TTL
field.help: TTL returned for answers coming from the hosts files.

field.label: Filter loopback
field.help: Ignore loopback addresses (127.0.0.0/8 and ::1) in the hosts files.

field.label: Refresh period
field.help: Interval at which hosts files are refreshed from their sources, e.g. 4h. Set to 0 to disable periodic refresh.

field.label: Loading strategy
field.help: How hosts files load at startup: blocking waits for all of them before serving, failOnError aborts startup if one fails to load, fast serves immediately and loads them in the background.

field.label: Max errors per source
field.help: Number of parse errors tolerated in a single hosts file before it is treated as invalid. Use -1 to disable the limit.

field.label: Load concurrency
field.help: Maximum number of hosts files processed in parallel.

field.label: Download timeout
field.help: Timeout for downloading each hosts file URL. Increase for large files or slow links, e.g. 60s.

field.label: Download attempts
field.help: Maximum number of download attempts for each hosts file URL (including the first attempt).

field.label: Download cooldown
field.help: Wait time between failed download attempts.

field.label: Download cache
field.help: Keep downloaded hosts files in /var/cache/blocky/hosts. Blocky then uses HTTP conditional requests to skip re-downloading unchanged files, and can serve a hosts file from disk when its source is temporarily unreachable. When off (default), downloads are stateless and nothing is written to disk.

field.label: Use ECS as client
field.help: Take the client address from the query's EDNS Client Subnet option instead of the sender's address, so a forwarder or proxy in front of Blocky does not appear as the client. Only a single-address option counts, /32 for IPv4 or /128 for IPv6; anything wider is ignored. The address is then used for client groups, client names and the query log.

field.label: Forward ECS
field.help: Forward the EDNS Client Subnet option to upstream resolvers.

field.label: IPv4 mask
field.help: Add an ECS option to IPv4 queries with this prefix length. 0 disables; maximum 32.

field.label: IPv6 mask
field.help: Add an ECS option to IPv6 queries with this prefix length. 0 disables; maximum 128.

field.label: Enable DNS64
field.help: Synthesize AAAA records from A records for IPv6-only clients behind a NAT64 gateway. Cannot be combined with AAAA in Drop query types above: those queries never reach DNS64, and Blocky exits at startup on that combination.

field.label: NAT64 prefixes
field.help: IPv6 prefixes used to synthesize AAAA records; empty uses the well-known 64:ff9b::/96. Lengths must be /32, /40, /48, /56, /64 or /96, and prefixes must not overlap, or Blocky exits at startup.

field.label: Exclusion set
field.help: IPv6 ranges that do not count as a real AAAA answer, so a response holding only these still gets synthesized. Empty uses the default set: IPv4-mapped ::ffff:0:0/96, loopback ::1/128, link-local fe80::/10, plus the prefixes above. A custom set replaces all of that, including the prefixes above, which must then be listed here to avoid synthesizing from an already synthesized address.

field.label: Address
field.help: Redis server as host:port, a unix socket path (starting with /), or (when using Sentinel) the master name. Lets multiple Blocky instances synchronize their cache and blocking state. Leave empty to disable Redis.

field.label: Username
field.help: Redis username (ACL), if required.

field.label: Password
field.help: Redis password, if required. It is never shown again; leave the field empty to keep the saved one. A value of file:/usr/local/etc/blocky/secrets/name reads it from that file instead, keeping it out of the OPNsense configuration and its backups.

field.label: Database
field.help: Redis database index.

field.label: Required
field.help: If enabled, Blocky refuses to start when the Redis connection cannot be established.

field.label: Connection attempts
field.help: Number of attempts to connect to Redis before giving up.

field.label: Connection cooldown
field.help: Wait time between Redis connection attempts.

field.label: Sentinel addresses
field.help: Redis Sentinel host:port entries for a high-availability setup. When at least one is set, the Address field above is treated as the Sentinel master name.

field.label: Sentinel username
field.help: Username used to authenticate to the Redis Sentinel hosts, if required.

field.label: Sentinel password
field.help: Password used to authenticate to the Redis Sentinel hosts, if required. It is never shown again; leave the field empty to keep the saved one. A value of file:/usr/local/etc/blocky/secrets/name reads it from that file instead, keeping it out of the OPNsense configuration and its backups.
